title: Salary Transparency: Clarity or Chaos?

reader_summary.headline: The earlier you think about putting a compensation structure in place.
reader_summary.overview: The earlier you think about putting a compensation structure in place, the stronger and healthier your company is because you have consistency, not fairness, consistency. You need to own the philosophy that you believe will drive the kinds of outcomes that you want as a company. There is a top 10% of your organization that isn't just the best performer, but they're critical.

key_points.text: What I mean by critical is if they left tomorrow, something stops working.

key_points.text: Ultimately, these laws are forcing companies to put the kind of infrastructure in place that a manager can use as the backstop.

key_points.text: Starting in 2016, states started enacting laws requiring employers to post their pay ranges.

thesis: The podcast argues that salary transparency laws are forcing companies to build consistent compensation infrastructure rather than relying on subjective fairness, as consistency provides the necessary backstop for managing pay discussions. It further states that many companies are currently struggling to catch up, with some adopting a wait-and-see approach or refusing to post salary ranges entirely.
